ov: Flippered marine mammals: the true seals, the sea lions and fur seals, and the walrus, 34 species in all. They eat at sea but come ashore to breed and rest.

why.et: Arctic Indigenous peoples have traditionally used the meat, blubber and skin of seals.
why.dg: Mainly the leopard seal: attacks are rare, but one killed a biologist snorkelling in Antarctica in 2003.

len: 1 m (Baikal seal) to 5 m (southern elephant seal)
wt: 45 kg (Baikal seal) to 3,200 kg (southern elephant seal)
rg: Oceans worldwide, mostly at sea but with a few species in fresh water, such as the Baikal seal.
df: Mainly fish and marine invertebrates. The leopard seal also hunts penguins and other seals, and walruses feed on the seabed.
